finding.title: Quota is check-then-consume with the consume after the upstream round trip: overshoot up to MaxConnections x unbounded tokens, and aborted/errored streams are never metered at all
finding.evidence: Check is a pure read with no reservation: quota.go:158 `qm.db.Where("id IN ? AND enabled = ?", ids, true).Find(&rows)` and quota.go:173 `if r.LimitValue > 0 && used >= r.LimitValue {`. It is called mid-pipeline at gateway.go:419 `if ok3, over := s.qm.Check(snap, apiKey.ID, ap.alias); !ok3 {`, while the increment happens only after the response is fully relayed: gateway.go:614 `s.qm.Consume(snap, ap.keyID, ap.alias, usage.Prompt, usage.Completion)` and gateway.go:768 (same call) - guarded by gateway.go:767 `if ap.status == "ok" || ap.status == "blocked" {`. Consume itself has a second, non-atomic reset branch at quota.go:196-198: `if now.After(q.ResetAt) {` ... `"used_value": delta, "reset_at": NextReset(q.Period, now)})` (an assignment, not an increment).
finding.impact: The TOCTOU window is the whole upstream round trip - up to DefaultTimeoutSeconds=120s for non-stream (gateway.go:498, settings.go:31) and unbounded for streams (gateway.go:492-505). Every request in flight when used == limit-1 is admitted, so a key whose quota is 1 request/day can spend ~MaxConnections=1000 requests (settings.go:32, the only admission control) in one burst; for token quotas the per-request delta is itself attacker-shaped because client max_tokens is not capped and streams are unbounded, so overshoot is effectively unlimited (1000 concurrent full-length completions billed to the operator). Worse, the control is not merely overshootable but bypassable: any stream that ends in a read error returns frFatal at gateway.go:726 with ap.status = "error", which fails the gateway.go:767 test, so the generated tokens are never added to used_value - an attacker loops 'start a large completion, disconnect at N KB' and consumes provider budget forever with a permanently empty quota counter. Finally, N concurrent requests that all take the expired-cycle branch overwrite each other (used_value = delta), so the counter under-counts even for successful traffic.
finding.recommendation: Reserve before forwarding: an atomic `UPDATE quotas SET used_value = used_value + :est WHERE id = ? AND (used_value + :est) <= limit_value` (estimate from the request body via tokens.Count) executed in the same step as Check, then reconcile the reservation with the real delta in Consume; make the lazy-reset branch an increment (`used_value = delta` only inside a `WHERE used_value = 0` guard or a transaction). Meter aborted streams too - call Consume with the accumulated usage on the scanner.Err()/early-return paths, since the upstream already produced and billed those tokens. Cap client max_tokens against an operator-set alias ceiling.
finding.mitigations_checked: the increment form at quota.go:201 `UpdateColumn("used_value", gorm.Expr("used_value + ?", delta))` is atomic in SQL (no read-modify-write in Go) for the non-reset branch; Check re-reads live DB values instead of trusting the snapshot (quota.go:158), so cross-restart persistence is fine; requests with delta <= 0 are skipped (quota.go:192-194); degrade-on-exceed (gateway.go:421-427) reduces cost but still admits unlimited requests to the degraded alias because the alias switch happens after Check and the new alias is never re-checked; there is no per-request or per-connection cost ceiling anywhere.

reason: Every quoted line was re-read end-to-end and is verbatim correct at the stated location. quota.go:148 is the Check signature; quota.go:158 and :173 are exactly as quoted - Check (148-179) performs a pure `Find` read and comparison with no reservation, lock, or write. gateway.go:419 (`if ok3, over := s.qm.Check(snap, apiKey.ID, ap.alias); !ok3 {`) is the only Check call site, and grep confirms the only two Consume call sites in production code are gateway.go:614 (forwardBuffered, after the full upstream body is read and written to the client at :611-612) and gateway.go:767-768 (`if ap.status == "ok" || ap.status == "blocked" {`). Therefore the TOCTOU window spans the entire upstream round trip: non-stream is bounded only by DefaultTimeoutSeconds, whose default 120 is verbatim at gateway.go:498 and settings.go:31; streams deliberately run with no total timeout (gateway.go:492-505, `ctx := c.Request.Context()` at :496 skips the WithTimeout block at :497-505). The admission ceiling is the global (not per-key) connection gauge at gateway.go:195, whose default MaxConnections=1000 is verbatim at settings.go:32; no default rate-limit rules or quotas are seeded anywhere (grep for seed/RateLimitRule{} finds only tests), and even operator-set rate limits bound requests/window, not the token delta. The delta is attacker-shaped: adapter.go:462-466 forwards client max_tokens verbatim with no ceiling (adapter.go:648 only applies a floor of 4096), and stream relay is unbounded, so one admitted burst can overshoot a token quota arbitrarily (the 16<<20 response cap at gateway.go:557 bounds only buffered non-stream responses per attempt). The never-metered path is real and reachable without any server bug: a stream that ends in a read error (including the error a canceled client context propagates into the upstream body read) hits gateway.go:719-727 - ap.status = "error" at :725, `return frFatal` at :726 - which fails the :767 gate, so usage accumulated at :755 is discarded; the same gate structure skips metering for upstream error events (:660-666) and for the non-stream disconnect chain (io.ReadAll fails at :557-561 -> frRetry -> all retries fail on the canceled ctx -> 502 at :472-476 with no Consume). The lazy-reset branch at quota.go:196-198 is indeed an assignment (`"used_value": delta`) not an increment, so concurrent expired-cycle consumers overwrite each other; worse, matchQuotas at quota.go:184 iterates the runtime snapshot, so q.ResetAt used at :196 can be up to HotReloadSeconds (default 3, settings.go:32) stale and clobber even the minute-ticker reset at quota.go:257-258. The degrade branch (gateway.go:421-427) swaps ap.alias after Check and never re-checks the degrade target's own quota, exactly as the original mitigations_checked states. No mitigation elsewhere in the flow closes any of these: SQLite serializes writes but not the read-then-consume window; Check re-reads live DB (correctly noted by the filer) but that only helps post-reset accuracy, not concurrency. Privilege model is sound: the attacker holds a valid API key, and the quota is the operator's sole billing guardrail against that key holder, so bypassing it is an authed-but-severe cost-exhaustion control failure - high, as filed. Minor precision notes that do not affect the verdict: (1) 'overshoot is effectively unlimited' is strictly true only for streams; a non-stream burst is bounded per attempt by the 16 MiB response read cap; (2) whether a client-canceled generation is actually billed by the upstream provider is provider-dependent (majority bill tokens produced up to cancellation, and non-stream generations generally complete server-side), but the TOCTOU burst component of the finding requires no disconnect and is fully code-supported regardless; (3) the EOF-without-finish case (gateway.go:728-732) does get metered as ok - an over-count, not exploitable.
exploit_sketch: Setup: attacker holds one valid gateway API key (sk-...) with, say, a 'requests=1/day' or 'tokens=100k/day' quota and a permissive rate-limit posture (none seeded by default). Attack A (burst overshoot): fire ~1000 concurrent streaming requests (the global MaxConnections cap is the only ceiling, gateway.go:195) with a long prompt and max_tokens=huge; every request executes Check (gateway.go:419) while used_value is still 0/low because no Consume has run yet (it happens only at gateway.go:614/:768 after full relay), so all 1000 are forwarded to the upstream provider and billed to the operator's provider keys - a '1 request per day' key spends ~1000 requests and the full token product of 1000 completions in one day. Attack B (permanent bypass): loop `curl -N --max-time 1 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -d '{"model":"<alias>","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<essay prompt>"}],"max_tokens":200000}'` - after 1s the client disconnects, the request context cancel propagates to the upstream body read, scanner.Err() fires at gateway.go:719, ap.status="error" (:725), `return frFatal` (:726) fails the `ap.status == "ok" || ap.status == "blocked"` gate (:767), so Consume never runs and used_value stays 0 forever - Check passes on every iteration while the upstream provider bills the partially generated completions. Repeat indefinitely. Attack C (accounting corruption): have N valid concurrent requests all land within the window after a period expires (or while the snapshot is up to 3s stale after the minute-ticker reset, quota.go:253-259); each takes quota.go:197-198 `Updates(map[string]any{"used_value": delta, ...})`, so the final used_value equals only the last request's delta - all other successful usage is silently erased from the billing counter.
